---
title: "Platforms and profiles"
# Thirteen columns across a platform, and a profile list opening under any of
# them. The default article column would scroll both sideways.
format:
  html:
    page-layout: full
# A report, not a notebook: an ordinary page has to hide its cells itself.
execute:
  echo: false
---

One product at a time, one row per platform: how many of its profiles were
published, and how the two flag sources line up across them. Click a platform
to list its profiles underneath it. The dashboard is where a single profile is
plotted; this page is for finding the platforms worth looking at, and the
profiles within them.

```{ojs}
//| output: false
// The same single module the other pages import. Resolving the specifier
// against document.baseURI keeps it working under any deployment path.
app = import(new URL("assets/js/app.js", document.baseURI).href)

catalog = app.loadCatalog()
variables = catalog.variables
statuses = catalog.statuses

// The categories where at least one source flagged the observation. The
// build marks them, so this page never has to name them.
flagged_statuses = statuses.filter((status) => status.flagged)

// The build copies profile times only when the input carries them, so the
// date columns are drawn only when there are dates to put in them.
has_time = {
  const columns = await app.profileColumns();
  return columns.includes("profile_timestamp");
}

// Per 1,000 published observations, so platforms of very different sizes can
// be compared. Null when there is nothing to divide by, rather than zero,
// which would read as "no disagreement".
function rate(count, observations) {
  return observations > 0 ? (1000 * count) / observations : null;
}

function perThousand(value) {
  return value === null || value === undefined ? "" : value.toFixed(1);
}

// A platform's first and last profile, to the day: the time of day says
// nothing about how long a platform has been reporting.
function day(value) {
  return app.formatTime(value).slice(0, 10);
}
```

::: {.nq-controls}

```{ojs}
viewof region = Inputs.select(catalog.regions, {
  label: "Region",
  format: (region) => region.name
})
```

```{ojs}
// The products of the chosen region only, so there is no pair to pick that
// does not exist. Changing the region starts again at its first product.
viewof product = Inputs.select(region.products, {
  label: "Product",
  format: (product) => product.name
})
```

```{ojs}
viewof variable = Inputs.select(variables, {
  label: "Variable",
  format: (variable) => variable.label
})
```

:::

```{ojs}
//| output: false
// All of the product's platforms at once: there are a few hundred at most, so
// the filter and the sort below run in the page rather than in a query per
// keystroke. The profiles are another matter and are fetched a page at a time
// when a platform is opened.
platforms = app.platformSummary(product.datasets, variables, statuses)
```

```{ojs}
{
  const profiles = platforms.reduce((sum, row) => sum + row.n_profiles, 0);
  const observations = platforms.reduce((sum, row) => sum + row.n_obs, 0);
  return htl.html`<p class="nq-meta">${region.name}, ${product.name}:
    <strong>${app.formatCount(platforms.length)}</strong> platforms,
    ${app.formatCount(profiles)} published profiles,
    ${app.formatCount(observations)} observations.</p>`;
}
```

```{ojs}
viewof platform_rows = Inputs.search(platforms, {
  columns: ["platform_code"],
  placeholder: "Platform code",
  label: "Platform"
})
```

```{ojs}
app.statusLegend(statuses)
```

```{ojs}
{
  const name = variable.name;
  const flagged = flagged_statuses;
  const dates = has_time
    ? [
        {
          key: "first_timestamp",
          label: "First",
          format: day,
          title: "The platform's first published profile"
        },
        {
          key: "last_timestamp",
          label: "Last",
          format: day,
          title: "The platform's last published profile"
        }
      ]
    : [];

  // The bar is over the flagged categories alone. Drawn over all five it
  // would be one grey block on every row, because a published profile is
  // mostly observations both sources call good.
  const shaped = platform_rows.map((row) => {
    const n_flagged = flagged.reduce((sum, s) => sum + row[`${name}_${s.key}`], 0);
    const n_disagree = row[`${name}_original_only`] + row[`${name}_aiqclib_only`];
    return {
      ...row,
      n_flagged,
      n_profiles_disagree: row[`${name}_n_profiles_disagree`],
      disagree_rate: rate(n_disagree, row.n_obs)
    };
  });

  return app.tableView(shaped, {
    columns: [
      {
        key: "platform_code",
        label: "Platform",
        align: "left",
        format: (value) => value
      },
      { key: "n_profiles", label: "Profiles", title: "Profiles published for this platform" },
      {
        key: "n_profiles_disagree",
        label: "Disagreeing",
        title: `Profiles with at least one ${variable.label.toLowerCase()} observation the two sources disagree on`
      },
      { key: "n_obs", label: "Observations", title: "Observations in those profiles" },
      ...dates,
      {
        key: "n_flagged",
        label: "Flagged mix",
        align: "left",
        title: "How the flagged observations split between the cases",
        render: (value, row) =>
          app.compositionBar(
            flagged.map((status) => ({
              label: status.label,
              value: row[`${name}_${status.key}`],
              color: status.color
            })),
            { empty: "nothing flagged on this platform" }
          )
      },
      ...statuses.map((status) => ({
        key: `${name}_${status.key}`,
        label: status.label,
        title: `${variable.label}: ${status.label.toLowerCase()}`
      })),
      {
        key: "disagree_rate",
        label: "Disagree per 1,000",
        format: perThousand,
        title:
          "Observations the two sources disagree on, per 1,000 published observations"
      }
    ],
    rowKey: "platform_code",
    sortKey: "disagree_rate",
    selectable: false,
    empty: platforms.length === 0
      ? "No profile of this product was published, so it has no platforms to list."
      : "No platform of this product matches.",
    // A platform's profiles, fetched a page at a time when it is opened: one
    // platform here runs to 8,541 of them. The same columns as the row above,
    // for one profile at a time, so a count in the platform's row can be
    // followed down to the profiles that make it.
    expand: (row) =>
      app.profileListView({
        columns: [
          {
            key: "profile_id",
            label: "Profile",
            align: "left",
            format: (value) => value
          },
          ...(has_time
            ? [{ key: "profile_timestamp", label: "Time", format: app.formatTime }]
            : []),
          { key: "n_obs", label: "Obs", title: "Observations in the profile" },
          ...statuses.map((status) => ({
            key: `${name}_n_${status.key}`,
            label: status.label,
            title: `${variable.label}: ${status.label.toLowerCase()}`
          })),
          {
            key: `${name}_n_disagree`,
            label: "Disagree",
            title: `${variable.label} observations the two sources disagree on`
          }
        ],
        rowKey: "profile_id",
        sortKey: `${name}_n_disagree`,
        pageSizes: [50, 200, 1000],
        pageSize: 50,
        searchable: false,
        selectable: false,
        empty: "No profile of this platform was published.",
        fetchRows: (request) =>
          app.profileSummary(product.datasets, {
            ...request,
            platform: row.platform_code
          }),
        countRows: (search) =>
          app.profileCount(product.datasets, search, row.platform_code)
      })
  });
}
```
